articleTitle: Electronic Dispersion Compensation Beyond 10 Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The dispersion tolerance in an optical transmission system tends to be proportional to the inverse square of the bit rate of the optical channel. A variety of methods have been used to compensate chromatic dispersion at 10 Gb/s with subsequent improvements in dispersion tolerance ranging from 800 ps/nm to 80,000 ps/nm, and also a range of circuit costs. At 40 and 100 Gb/s not only is the impact of dispersion more stringent, but the circuit challenges are also severe. In this presentation we will discuss the scaling of electronic dispersion compensation methods to 40 and 100 Gb/s, and show full dispersion compensation in a 40 Gb/s product.

articleTitle: Coherent Equalization versus Direct Detection for 111-Gb/s Ethernet Transport
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We discuss coherent equalization to realize robust 111-Gb/s transmission. For 111-Gb/s POLMUX-RZ-DQPSK we experimentally show the advantage of coherent equalization over direction detection for compensation of both chromatic dispersion and differential group delay.

articleTitle: Systematic Investigation of Nematic Liquid Crystal Mixtures at 30 GHz
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper various nematic liquid crystal mixtures are investigated at 30 GHz. The used cavity perturbation characterization method enables the precise extraction of permittivity and dielectric losses. The three investigated matrices show a strong influence in the material quality factor eta, defined as the ratio between the tunability tau and the maximum dielectric losses tandelta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>, ranging between etaap3.2 ... 12.5.

articleTitle: 100G Ethernet A Review of Serial Transport Options
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review recently demonstrated options for serial transport technologies at 100 Gb/s, including binary, multi-level, and coherently detected polarization-multiplexed formats.

articleTitle: Techniques for Photonic Generation of Millimeter-Wave Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper reviews various photonic techniques available for the generation of millimeter wave signals, including by direct modulation of lasers, injection locking, beat frequency sources with phase-locked loops, dual wavelength lasers and femtosecond lasers.

articleTitle: PDL-Tolerant Real-time Polarization-Multiplexed QPSK Transmission with Digital Coherent Polarization Diversity Receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a real-time electronic polarization tracking algorithm which enables robust optical polarization-multiplexed synchronous quadrature phase shift keying transmission with DFB lasers. The achieved BER at a data rate of 2.8 Gbit/s is well below the FEC threshold.

articleTitle: Towards Robust 100G Ethernet Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We discuss transmission requirements for commercially deployable, robust 100 G Ethernet transport. Coherently equalised POLMUX-RZ-DQPSK is shown to be both compatible with 10 G infrastructure and suitable for long-haul transmission.

articleTitle: Pre-Emphasis and RF-Pilot Tone Phase Noise Compensation for Coherent OFDM Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, pre-emphasis and RF-pilot tone phase noise compensation are discussed for coherent OFDM transmission systems. It is shown that only 1.6% of the total power is required for the RF-pilot for optimal phase noise compensation.

articleTitle: Optofluidic Microring Dye Laser
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrated, for the first time, an optofluidic microring dye laser on a monolithic poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) chip. Laser threshold of 9.2 nJ was obtained with a single mode liquid-core waveguide based microring cavity.

articleTitle: Agile Wideband Light Source for Optical Coherence Tomography Using Optical SSB Frequency Sweep Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We propose an agile wideband light source, which targeted on optical coherence tomography (OCT), consists of an optical single-sideband modulation (SSB) frequency sweeper cascaded with an optical frequency comb generator and a multi-wavelength light source.

articleTitle: Compensation of coherent DQPSK receiver imperfections
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper studies the impact of imperfections and impairments on the performance of a coherent phase-diversity DQPSK receiver. Experiments demonstrate that quadrature imbalance can be corrected by ellipse fitting and Gram-Schmidt-like orthogonalization. In addition, it is shown that intermediate frequency offset can be estimated using low complexity, feed-forward, least-square-error based algorithms.

articleTitle: Optical Homodyne Receiver Comprising Phase and Polarization Diversities with Digital Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper describes a coherent optical receiver, where drifts of the carrier phase and state of polarization are estimated with digital signal processing. The complex amplitude of the signal is entirely restored with such receiver.

articleTitle: Photoreceivers for 100 Gbit/s Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Waveguide integrated photodetectors with 100 GHz bandwidth were developed. Different transmission experiments have demonstrated their capability for 107 Gbit/s applications. Design and results for separately packaged photodiodes and co-packaged receivers with 1 x 2 demultiplexer are shown.

articleTitle: Myths and Truths about Optical OFDM
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is currently discussed as an attractive format to overcome physical impairments in spectrally efficient optical communication links such as modal dispersion, chromatic dispersion and polarization mode dispersion. This paper reviews recent progress in the field.

articleTitle: Transmission Systems beyond 100 Gbit/s: Status and Technologies
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report on single-channel transmission systems with data rates beyond 100 Gbit/s. The current status and the applied technologies are reviewed, in particular 160-Gbit/s-based systems with long transmission distances and high bit-rates using advanced modulation formats.

articleTitle: Implementation Aspects of High-Speed DSP for Transmitter and Receiver Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Today's electronic processing capability means that it is now possible to perform extensive signal processing on signals at the highest data rates. In this presentation we discuss the design choices available to the DSP designer.

articleTitle: Chromatic Dispersion Compensation using LDPC-Coded Turbo Equalization
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present an iterative equalization scheme suitable for compensation of chromatic dispersion. This scheme is able to compensate for chromatic dispersion over 800 km of standard SMF in an NRZ optical transmission system without optical dispersion compensation operating at 10 Gb/s for only 128 states in corresponding trellis description of the channel.

articleTitle: Electronics Produced by Roll-to-roll Self-Aligned Imprint Lithography
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this presentation, we present a method for fabrication using self-aligned imprint lithography (SAIL). The self-aligned process solves the layer-to-layer registration issues arising from the dimensionally changes of flexible substrates. The imprint process eliminates the need for photolithography and greatly lowers the cost for large area electronics because it is compatible with roll-to-roll processing. The basic concepts of the SAIL process are presented along with electrical characteristics of devices produced by roll-to-roll SAIL processes.

articleTitle: Microwave Frequency Generation up to 27.5 GHz Using a Dual-Wavelength Brillouin Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate microwave frequency generation up to 27.5 GHz using a dual-wavelength stimulated Brillouin fiber laser. We discuss advantages and limitations of this device as a microwave/millimeter-wave low phase noise oscillator.

articleTitle: Terabit OTDM transmission Key challenges
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report recent progress and key challenges for terabit/s OTDM transmission. We focus especially on emerging ultrahigh-speed transmission technologies such DPSK and DQPSK transmission and a distortion-free transmission scheme using time-domain optical Fourier transformation.

articleTitle: Large-area replication technology for the production of electrical-optical circuit boards (EOCB)
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A large-area (390 mmtimes150 mm) replication technology for polymer optical waveguides is presented. SU-8 casting moulds are used for the fabrication of polysiloxane (PDMS) based optical waveguides. The waveguides show low optical loss and high thermal, mechanical and environmental stability.

articleTitle: 40G-OTN FEC Framer LSI Enabling Coding for Advanced Modulation Formats and 4 × 1OGbE Transparent Multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: OTN functions-integrated LSI offers several functions to support 40G-DWDM systems: 2 kinds of 40G FECs, OTN/SDH/10GE-LAN processing, and coding for advanced modulation formats. 4 times 10GE-LAN transparently multiplexed DQPSK transmission is successfully conducted.

articleTitle: The potential of high speed UTC-TW photo detectors to generate sub-MM wave signals-predictions by a new analytical model
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This study presents a novel model of a high-speed uni-travelling-carrier travelling wave (UTC-TW) photo detector for submillimeter wave signal generation. The model is fully analytical and is intended to be used as a design tool. This newly designed photo detector can operate well above 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Proposed Applications of 3-D Optical Interconnect Technologies to Integrated Chemical Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We propose integrated photonic/electronic/chemical system (IPECS) based on 3-D optical interconnect technologies, including 3-D optical circuits. Self-organized lightwave network (SOLNET). Resource-saving heterogeneous integration process (PL-Pack with SORT), and molecular layer deposition (MLD), for energy/bio applications.

articleTitle: Review of Recent Progress in MLSE Receiver Technologies
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: MLSE offers adaptive non-linear receiver-sided equalization for channels with memory. New areas of application considered are directly modulated DFB laser, D(B/Q)PSK, and duo-binary transmission systems. Reduced computational complexity is a new research area.

articleTitle: An Exact Analysis of RZ-vs. NRZ-DPSK Performance in ASE Noise Limited High Speed Optical Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The back-to-back performance of optical RZ-DPSK and NRZ-DPSK formats was compared using KLSE method. The effect of unmatched optical bandpass filter was studied with/without the presence of the electrical low pass filter in the receiver.

articleTitle: Systematic Design and Simulation of Polymer Microring Resonators with the Combination of Beam Propagation Method and Matrix Model
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper, a basic microring resonator structure is divided into two separate regions, i.e. a 4-port coupler and a 2-port ring/curved waveguide, thus can be regarded as an optical system composed of two components.

articleTitle: Ultra Long-Haul QPSK Transmission using a Digital Coherent Receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Digital coherent receivers have enabled ultra-long haul transmission of QPSK data. We outline the principles behind such receivers which have allowed 42.8 Gbit/s data to be transmitted over 6400 km of standard fiber without optical dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: High Speed Arbitrary Waveform Generation and Processing using a Photonic Digital-to-Analog Converter
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper we report on our recent progress in using photonic digital-analog converters for arbitrary waveform generation. Optical arbitrary waveforms are generated using a time-domain approach based on an interfere metric modulator device.

articleTitle: Present Status of the Development of the Yb Optical Lattice Clock at NMIJ/AIST
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The present status of the development of the Yb optical lattice clock at NMIJ and future prospects are presented.

articleTitle: Micro- and Nanobiological Systems: New Technologies and Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Summary form only given. Nanotechnology has recently been applied to a wide range of biological systems. In particular, there is a current push to examine the interface between the biological world and micro/nano-scale systems. In this paper, the author presents ongoing work in microfluidics, biosensors, and nano-bio interfaces. Specific topics are included in the development of a DNA-based, microfluidic detection system and its use for both pathogen identification and forensic DNA analysis. In addition, the author covers current studies in magnetic-microfluidic integration, bacterial quorum sensing, bacterial adhesion, and novel optical detection systems. Some of the unique biological considerations for these systems are discussed, as well as issues relating to device fabrication and testing.

articleTitle: QPSK with Coherent Detection over Ultra-Long Distance Improved by Nonlinearity Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Coherent detection Is very promising for improving the capacity and reach of transmission systems. Assuming QPSK format, its performance is compared at 40 Gbit/s and after 3,060 km, with differential detection, and improved by mitigating nonlinearities digitally.

articleTitle: Electronic Dispersion Compensation Based on Maximum-Likelihood Sequence Estimation for 10 Gb/s Fiber-Optic Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present a two-fold oversampling maximum-likelihood-sequence-estimation receiver for 10 Gb/s fiberoptic communication systems. We use the Volterra theory to model the channel nonlinearity, and least mean square algorithm to update the channel characteristics without training sequence.

articleTitle: Hybrid Electro-Optic Polymer Devices: Beating the Drive Voltage/Insertion Loss Trade-Off
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We have developed a solution to the voltage/insertion loss tradeoff in electro-optic polymer modulators by adopting hybrid geometry. We will discuss recent results in these devices, notably the achievement of r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub> = 170 pm/V in a device.

articleTitle: Optofluidic Technologies
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Optofluidics refers to adaptive systems that integrate optical and fluidic devices. Micro and nano-fluidics enable novel devices which introduce liquids into optical structures. We discuss recent optofluidic developments, including optically powered vapor pumps.

articleTitle: Singal-to-noise Ratio Enhancement Using 3-D Sensing Filaments in Structure-Induced Micro Fluid Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We analyze signal-to-noise ratio enhancement of sensing filament array considering micro turbulence induced when fluid flows through its three-dimensional structure. Combined with surface area, a factor of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> can be expected compared to 2-D sensing array, making it possible to sense ultra-low concentration contents in fluid flow.

articleTitle: UV-based Nano Imprint Fabrication of Gold Grating Couplers on Silicon-on-Insulator
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Fiber-to-waveguide gold grating couplers are fabricated using UV-based nano imprint lithography and lift-off on top of an unprocessed silicon-on-insulator chip. Over 22% efficiency and a 1 dB bandwidth of 36 nm is demonstrated in the telecom band.

articleTitle: High Power (> 150 mW) Electrically Pumped Semiconductor Modelocked Lasers at 1550 nm with Pulse Widths Approaching 6 ps
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report on the generation of stable modelocked pulses from electrically pumped monolithic semiconductor diode lasers with repetition rates > 5 GHz, pulse widths approaching 6 ps, and output powers exceeding 150 mW.

articleTitle: Slab-Coupled Optical Waveguide Devices for Low-Noise Signal Generation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review the use of slab-coupled optical waveguide amplifiers (SCOWAs) in low-noise mode-locked and single-frequency lasers. We also report a new single-frequency laser cavity incorporating an Er/Yb-codoped waveguide distributed-Bragg-reflector that produces 330-mW power with 75-kHz linewidth.

articleTitle: Combined nanoimprint and photolithography of integrated polymer optics
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate wafer-scale fabrication by combined nanoimprint and photolithography (CNP) of integrated polymer optics, combining active and passive polymer components with nm to mm features. Distributed feed-back (DFB) polymer dye lasers are integrated with polymer waveguides. The laser devices are defined in SU-8 resist, doped with Rhodamine 6G laser dye, shaped as planar slab waveguides on a Fused Silica buffer substrate, and with a lst-order DFB surface corrugation forming the laser resonator. When optically pumped at 532 nm, lasing is obtained in the wavelength range 560 nm -600 nm, determined by the grating period. Our results, where 20 laser devices are defined across a 10 cm diameter wafer substrate, demonstrate the feasibility of CNP for wafer-scale fabrication of advanced nano-structured active and passive polymer optical components.

articleTitle: All-optical Signal Processing for Ultra-high Speed Photonic Network
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Ultra-high speed all-optical signal processing for photonic networks is discussed. Using a fiber-based optical switch, ultra-high speed amplitude noise suppression and all-optical format conversion of OOK to PSK are presented.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion compensation effectiveness of an MLSE-EDC receiver for three variants of duobinary
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Experimental data is obtained on the compensation effectiveness of MLSE-EDC against chromatic dispersion for three variants of the duobinary modulation format. The MLSE technology offers the greatest dispersion tolerance advantage for the optical duobinary format.

articleTitle: Photonic Integrated Circuits fabricated by Deep UV and Hot Embossing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review our work in the field of deep UV modification of methacrylate-based polymers. Planar and rib waveguide structures are presented. A method of integrating polymer waveguides with organic light sources into all-polymer systems is shown.

articleTitle: Polarization-Mode-Dispersion Impairments and Mitigation in Ultra-High Speed Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review the polarization-mode-dispersion (PMD) induced penalty and PMD mitigation techniques in fiber-optic transmission systems. Recent progress in PMD mitigation techniques that could enable ultra-high speed fiber-optic transmission is discussed.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Soft-decision FEC Receivers
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present threshold tracking of a soft-decision based forward error correction system as an application of digital signal processing for optical communications. The 3-bit soft-decision thresholds are closely controlled to obtain the best possible error-correction performance.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Replicated Polymer Optical Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The manufacturing technology of polymer optical waveguide called SPICA (stacked polymer optical IC/advanced) utilizing a unique replication process is presented. The performance of the single mode waveguide and the film type waveguide both at characteristic of a practical use level are discussed.

articleTitle: Monitoring Fluorescence in Cultured Neural Networks using Polymer Waveguide Excitation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present fluorescence excitation of cultured living neural cells using integrated optical waveguides. The waveguides (width 5, 7, 9 mum) are fabricated in polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) using deep ultraviolet radiation. The excitation wavelength is 473 nm.

articleTitle: Optofluidic Intracavity Spectroscopy of Canine Lymphoma and Lymphocytes
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Intracavity transmission spectra of single canine lymphoma cells are distinct from noncancerous lymphocytes. An effective index model yields a nuclear size vs. refractive index relationship and clarifies the impact of mode confinement on wavelength shift.

articleTitle: Advanced Modulation Format for 100-Gbit/s Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper discusses advanced modulation formats for the realization of single-channel 100-Gbit/s transmission in optical fiber communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization for 80 Gb/s NRZ-DPSK Transceiver with Pre-Emphasized Electrical Signal Driving Path
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Employing a rigorous KLSE based quasi-analytical method for the BER calculation, we optimize an 80 Gb/s NRZ-DPSK transceiver by pre-emphasizing the high frequency portion of the gain shape of electrical signal driving path.

articleTitle: 16-QAM Signal Design and Detection in Presence of Nonlinear Phase Noise
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Constellation design and coherent detection of 16-QAM signals in the presence of nonlinear phase noise are studied. Various decision strategies and phase-noise mitigation techniques are compared in terms of symbol-error rate performance.

articleTitle: Simple Method for MLSE Performance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present a novel semi-analytic technique to estimate the performance of MLSE receivers. The technique offers an intuitive explanation for the difference in performance between an MLSE receiver and an ISI-free threshold receiver.

articleTitle: Fundamental Limits on the Performance of Maximum-Likelihood Sequence Estimation in Dispersive Optical Links
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: MLSE experiments supporting 10 Gbit/s, 1000 km uncompensated G.652 fiber transmission, have been successfully performed. However, a residual 2 dB OSNR-penalty, nonlinear effects and Viterbi processor complexity may constitute fundamental limitations to actual MLSE exploitation in long-haul links.

Index Terms: Performance Of The Maximum Likelihood Estimator

articleTitle: Soft Lithographic Fabrication of Microresonators
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Using ultra-high-Q toroid microcavity masters, soft lithography is applied to fabricate polymer microcavity arrays with Q factors in excess of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> . This technique produces resonators with material-limited quality factors.

articleTitle: Integrated Terahertz Biophotonics: Terahertz Spectroscopy of Proteins in Microfluidic Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We measure the absorption spectrum of bovine serum albumin in aqueous solutions at terahertz frequencies using microfluidic channels. The data agrees well with previous results and demonstrates the feasibility of terahertz biosensing in microfluidic devices.

articleTitle: Entangled and correlated two-photon absorption effects of an organic material
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Entanglement is one of the most fundamental and significant features in quantum mechanics. The spatial parameters of the correlated photon pairs were investigated in order to improve the entanglement property within the correlated photon flux. The focus of the work is to utilize the properties of entanglement and novel materials to produce new sensitive detection schemes. Through this focus, we demonstrated one of the most important applications of quantum effects, namely entangled two-photon absorption spectroscopy.

articleTitle: The Yb and Ca Standards: Approaches to High Stability, High Accuracy, and Transportable Optical Atomic Clocks
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This talk presents two different types of neutral atom optical clocks and emphasizes the systems' differences in potential performance and complexity. Approaches in attaining high stability, high accuracy, and transportable optical atomic clocks are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Er- and Yb-doped Fiber Laser Frequency Combs and Their Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Progress in femtosecond fiber laser based frequency combs is reviewed. Recent examples of Er-fiber frequency combs with sub-Hz relative comb tooth linewidths and Yb-frequency combs with > 10 W average power will be discussed.

articleTitle: Self-Formed Functional Polymer Wires Mimicking Filament Structure in Aquatic Respiration System for Intravascular In-vivo Bio-chemical Sensing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Mimicking filament structure commonly found in aquatic respiration system, we report a self-formed, self-assembled three-dimensional optical waveguide polymer wire suitable to form massive sensing array to enhance bio-chemical sensitivity in intravascular environments.

articleTitle: High Data Rate Submarine Transmission Systems: Getting to and beyond 40 Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This talk will discuss high data rate transmission over transoceanic distance. First, we will discuss issues specific to submarine transmission systems, then look at 40 G, and finally discuss the technologies that might enable even higher rates.

articleTitle: Narrow Linewidth 1.5 μm sources and the Thermal Limit
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A measured 1 Hz linewidth between a cavity-stabilized, 1535 nm cw fiber laser and the 1535-nm tooth of a stabilized fiber frequency comb is below the thermodynamic limit of the frequency comb.

articleTitle: Pitfalls when Modeling High-Speed Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present methods for accurately modeling high-speed optical transmission systems with channel data rates beyond 40 Gbit/s. We provide simulation guidelines and examples for investigating limitations of transmitter and receiver, fiber impairments, and estimating signal performances.

articleTitle: 5-GHz optical arbitrary waveform generation using > 100 independently controlled spectral lines from a compressed phase-modulated CW laser comb
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate high-fidelity optical arbitrary waveform generation via spectral line-by-line shaping on more than 100 spectral comb lines selected from a compressed phase-modulated CW laser frequency comb with 5 GHz line spacing.

articleTitle: Generation of High Repetition Rate Femtosecond Pulse Trains with a High Finesse External Fabry-Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Generation of 130-fs pulse trains at 1560 nm with 1 GHz repetition rate is demonstrated by locking a fundamentally mode-locked 200 MHz repetition rate fiber laser to a high finesse (F=2100) external Fabry-Perot cavity.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Time Scale Transformation and Recording Utilizing Parametric Temporal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Parametric temporal imaging enables real time transformation of ultrafast waveforms to a time scale accessible by convention recording instruments. Principles and the development of this technology will be reviewed along with recent experimental results.

articleTitle: Iterative Decodable Block-Codes for High-Speed Optical Transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this invited paper, we compare performance of three classes of iterative decodable codes suitable for use in highspeed optical transmission systems: (i) turbo product codes (TPCs), (ii) low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, and (iii) generalized LDPC (GLDPC) codes with Hamming, BCH or Reed-Muller component codes.

articleTitle: A spectrum-efficient 80-Gbit/s DPSK transmitter using phase interleaving technology without optical-time or polarization-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a cost-effective 80-Gbit/s DPSK transmitter using phase interleaving without optical-time/polarization-division multiplexing. Two cascaded independent 40-Gbit/s modulations are time-interleaved to generate 80-Gbit/s DPSK with high spectrum efficiency: 20-dB bandwidth of only 0.68 nm.

articleTitle: Optical frequency transfer over 38 km of installed fiber at less than 3 × 10-19 residual fractional instability
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We transmit a narrow-linewidth cw laser at 1535 nm across 38 km of installed fiber. Through standard Doppler-cancellation techniques, we achieve a residual fractional frequency instability of 4 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup> at 1 second averaging time.

articleTitle: UV-embossed polymer optical bench for integration of polymer waveguide devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: For optical-electrical (O/E) integration of polymer waveguide devices, a polymer optical bench with embedded-electric-circuits was developed and realized by using the UV-embossing technology. An upside-down mounted polymer waveguide device showed not only more efficient fiber-chip coupling but also a good electrical contact.

articleTitle: 8OGb/s-256QAM Format using Phase Noise Tolerant Pilot Carrier Aided Homodyne Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We investigated the phase noise-tolerance of coherent detection in a high-efficiency optical fiber transmission using 256-QAM formats at 80 Gb/s by computer simulation. We confirmed that the proposed scheme has a phase noise tolerance with DGD.

articleTitle: QAM based coherent transmission technologies using DSP
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Recent progress on QAM coherent transmission is described. QAM transmission started at 20 Msymbol/s, 64-128 QAM, and recently reached 1 Gsymbol/s, 64 QAM, carrying 12 Gbit/s data in a 2 GHz optical bandwidth.

articleTitle: Nanofluidic Devices for Rapid Analysis of DNA and Proteins
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A new class of nanofluidic filter array devices were designed and fabricated to perform rapid separation (both analytical and preparative) of DNA and proteins covering very broad biological size scales. By virtue of its separation efficiency, gel-free operation, ease of sample recovery and high throughput, these nanofluidic filter array devices hold great promise for an integrated biomolecule sample preparation and analysis system.

articleTitle: Nanoimprint and nano-machining process for tunable hollow waveguide devices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present the fabrication of circular grating based on nanoimprint and nano-machining process. We successfully demonstrate the nanoimprint of circular grating with pitch of 780 nm for large-area tunable hollow waveguide devices.

articleTitle: Challenges in Test and Measurement for 100GE serial TDM system studies
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This presentation seeks to address some key test and measurement issues currently facing the R&D community investigating the feasibility of serial 100Gb Ethernet as a viable next generation high speed data communication solution.

articleTitle: Microwave photonic frequency multiplication for a tunable millimeter and terahertz CW signal generator with improved spurious characteristics
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This report presents the microwave photonic frequency multiplication technique for CW MM/THz-wave generations which provides not only high frequency accuracy and stability, but also broadband continuous frequency tunability and high spurious signal suppression.

articleTitle: Implementation Tolerances for Coherent Analog Links Using I/Q Detection and Digital Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We experimentally and numerically investigate practical implementation considerations for highly linear photonic links based on in-phase and quadrature detection with demodulation using digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Subwavelength Optical Elements and Nanoimprint Technology for Optical System on Chip
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this paper an optical system is integrated on a chip and fabricated monolithically. The two new platform technologies besides guided-wave integrated optics are discussed. Subwavelength optical elements (SOEs), a new class of optical devices well suited for wafer level integration, and nanoimprint technology an enabling nanopatterning method. To fabricate SOEs and harvest their potentials, a ultra-high-resolution large-area nanopatterning with high-throughput and low-cost is essential. Among all available nanopatterning methods, nanoimprint lithography (NIL), demonstrated appears to be one of the most promising technology for SOE fabrication.

articleTitle: Novel sensor architecture for high-throughput and high-sensitivity biomolecular interaction analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Traditional label-free sensors for biomolecular interaction sensing suffer from two principal shortcomings: poor sensitivity vis-a-vis labeled techniques, and limited throughput. To overcome these shortcomings, we developed a novel sensor based on the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) phenomenon. The sensor can detect up to 110 simultaneous independent interactions at 10 Hz with a root-mean-square noise level of 2.6 times 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> RIU/Hz05. This noise level is lower than that of any commercial SPR instrument, even those offering minimal or no multiplexing. Using simple software controls, the user can improve the sensitivity further by reducing the available measurement range or level of multiplexing.

articleTitle: A Non-invasive Dual-Channel Oximeter based on Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS)
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) has been used as non-invasive sensor of blood oxygen level. In this paper, we demonstrate our implementation of a compact dual-channel blood-oxygen level monitoring system based on NIRS.

articleTitle: Microstructure, Charge Transport and Trapping in Anisotropic Polymeric Thin Film Transistors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: In this work we have used the directional solidification of a crystallizing solvent to further manipulate the microstructure of P3HT thin films, controlling the orientation and size of the disordered grain boundary regions. Resulting films have a very anisotropic distribution of grain boundaries in the plane of the substrate, with periodic crystalline regions. By fabricating thin film transistors with these anisotropic films, and subsequently fitting temperature dependent mobility data to the Mobility Edge Model, we have means to explore the relationship between trap density within grain boundaries and charge transport.

articleTitle: A High Sensitivity Surface Plasmon Resonance Configuration based on the Phase Retardation Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A high sensitivity surface plasmon resonance (SPR) configuration based on the phase retardation between the p and s polarization is proposed. The new configuration can achieve as high sensitivity as the phase detection approach by utilizing the intensity detection method. Experimental result shows the feasibility of this new configuration.

articleTitle: Atomic Frequency Standards and their Impact on the Past, Present and Future of the Second
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Due to the rapid progress in optical frequency standards with uncertainties approaching and even surpassing the best present caesium primary standards it is foreseeable, that the second might be redefined in the future. I will present a history of optical frequency standards and discuss the prospects and possible applications of improved clocks.

articleTitle: Briadbabd 3D Integrated Optics in Photonic Band Gap Materials
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Summary form only given. Photonic band gap (PBG) materials are artificial, periodic, dielectrics that enable engineering of the most fundamental properties of electromagnetic waves. These include the laws of refraction, diffraction, and spontaneous emission of light. Unlike traditional semiconductors that rely on the propagation of electrons through an atomic lattice. PBG materials execute their novel functions through selective trapping or "localization of light". Three dimensional (3D) PBG materials offer a unique opportunity to simultaneously (i) synthesize micron-scale 3D optical circuits that do not suffer from diffractive losses and (ii) engineer the electromagnetic vacuum density of states in this 3D optical micro-chip. The 3D PBG enables broadband on-chip optical communication in fully three-dimensional optical micro-circuits. Unlike traditional wave-guides that confine light in a high refractive index core by total internal reflection, the circuit paths in a PBG material may consist of air. They guide light through wave interference effects, the hallmark of the localization phenomenon. In the case of the PBG optical circuit, there are three geometrical dimensions for device integration and an additional dimension of frequency bandwidth, whereby hundreds of optical wavelength channels of information can be conveyed in parallel through a single PBG wave-guide. I review recent approaches to micro-fabrication of photonic crystals with a large 3D PBG centered near 1.5 microns. These include direct laser-writing techniques, holographic lithography, silicon double inversion, and a newly invented optical phase mask lithography technique.

articleTitle: Polymeric composite materials for optical data storage and processing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Novel holographic materials have been developed to be used in optical devices for storage and processing. This article reports on the results of an extended investigation performed on the preparation and optical characterization of novel polymeric composites suitable for holographic patterning, where one and two-dimensional periodic structures have been recorded and investigated.

articleTitle: Direct two-photon resonant excitation and absolute frequency measurement of cesium transitions using a femtosecond comb
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We measure the optical transition frequencies of the 6s <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub> rarr 8s <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>, 9s <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sub>, and 7d <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2,5/2</sub> transitions in a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>Cs vapor cell, with an uncertainty < 100 kHz using a femtosecond laser frequency comb.

articleTitle: Ethernet Evolution: The Path to 100 Gigabit Ethernet
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The ongoing development and deployment of a single seamless converged network responsible for the transmission of voice, video, and data through wireline and wireless applications is creating a complex eco-system. Ethernet has expanded beyond its traditional LAN roots, and is now everywhere. This has resulted in an ecosystem in which IP-based content and applications are transported seamlessly between carriers, enterprises, and consumers through a fabric of Ethernet-based networks.

articleTitle: Photodetection and Photovoltaic Properties of Polymer Composite Materials Based on Pentacene and Carbon Nanotube
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An IR active photodetector device consisting of poly(vinyl carbazole) (PVK), PbSe quantum dot and single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNT) has been constructed. Efficient collection of IR photons in our devices followed by fast charge transfer and enhanced conduction in the polymer and SWNT networks results in a maximum EQE of ~2.6%.

articleTitle: Porphyrin-Based Molecular Wires
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Conjugated porphyrin oligomers exhibit extraordinary third-order nonlinear optical properties, such as strong two-photon absorption, non-linear refraction and reverse-saturable absorption, leading to potential applications in areas such as photodynamic therapy, optical data storage, fluorescence imaging, all-optical computing and optical power limiting. This presentation will illustrate how supramolecular self-assembly can be used to control the photophysics of these jr-systems, via supramolecular control of the conformation, through the synthesis of structures such as the double-strand ladder and cyclic octamer nanoring.

articleTitle: Measurement of Acetylene-d Absorption Lines with a Self-Referenced Fiber Laser Frequency Comb
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper employed a self-referenced fiber laser frequency comb (FFC) to create a reference atlas of transitions of another acetylene isotope whose band covers the C-band telecom spectrum from 195 to 198 THz. Using the FFC together with a cavity-based diode laser-saturation-absorption spectrometer, this uncertainty is reduced to less than 2 kHz. It is concluded that the self-referenced fiber laser comb provides a very reliable and straightforward system by which large numbers of reference frequencies can be measured.

articleTitle: Quantitative Measurement of the Dynamics of a Mode-locked Laser
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The linear response of a mode-locked laser to a perturbation of the pump power is measured quantitatively. Relaxation oscillations, frequency pulling, and nonlinear changes in the timing and phase of the pulse train are observed.

articleTitle: Excitons in Biological and Non-Biological Nano-Structured Systems: Progress Towards Bio-inspired Photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An exciton, an elementary excitation formed from a bound electron-hole pair, is the lowest optically excited state in semiconductors, and plays a prominent role in condensed matter physics. In reduced dimensional materials, including biological structures, excitonic transitions should dominate due to carrier confinement. Here, I will first describe excitonic transitions in the photocurrent spectra of carbon nanotube diodes as a model system to describe optical absorption in ID semiconductors. The sharp narrow peaks are associated with excitonic transitions, and peak # 1 corresponds to the lowest optically allowed exciton state. The observation of sharp narrow absorption peaks at room temperature in a semiconductor is unprecedented, and is due to strong optical transitions of excitons as compared to band-to-band transitions normally seen for bulk materials.

articleTitle: Super-Stable Optical Comb and Pulse Generation Using Electro-Optic Modulation
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We review a simple and highly-stable ultra-flat frequency comb generator employing a single-stage electro-optic Mach-Zehnder modulator. Synthesis of a picosecond/sub-picosecond pulse train from the frequency comb using linear/nonlinear pulse compression technique is also reported.

articleTitle: Implantable Multichannel Silicon-based neural probe
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A kind of silicon oxide based multi-channel neural probe array is reported. It has four shafts and twenty recording sites. Processes to fabricate the microelectrode and test results were described.

articleTitle: A Waveguide Biosensors Local Evanescent Field Response to an Immunoassay Complex
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A compact photonic immunoassay biosensor that can simultaneously sense multiple analytes has been implemented. NSOM results indicate 8% modulation of the local evanescent field due to an 18 nm biological adlayer on the waveguide's surface.

articleTitle: High-speed all-optical signal processing techniques for high-speed optical transmission
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper reviews recent progress on high-speed all-optical signal processing technologies including switching and regeneration for optical transmission systems.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Optical Components for Light Management by UV Embossing
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The trend towards miniaturization in optics holds the promise of a growth analog to that of microelectronics. Thanks to manufacturing and material advances, high-quality micro-optic components now compete with conventional optics in many applications, including consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Novel 100Gbps Ethernet Systems for Next-generation Metro Transport and Wide-area Access Networks using Optical carrier suppression and separation Technique
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A novel, dispersion tolerant, spectrally efficient scheme of transmitting 100 Gbps per wavelength channel by exploiting optical carrier suppression and separation technique and optical duobinary or DQPSK modulation is proposed and evaluated through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Optical Arbitrary Pulse Train Generation via Spectral Line-by-Line Pulse Shaping
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate optical arbitrary pulse generation using spectral line-by-line shaping on a mode-locked fiber laser. The pulse train within each period can be independently controlled as specified.

articleTitle: Increasing the Mode-Spacing of Stabilized Frequency Combs with Optical Filter Cavities
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We explore methods and limitations for increasing the mode spacing of a 1 GHz optical frequency comb using a Fabry-Perot filter cavity. Applications to optical and microwave waveform generation are highlighted.

articleTitle: Large-Scale, Long-Term Stable Femtosecond Timing Distribution and Synchronization Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate large-scale, long-term stable, and femtosecond-precision timing distribution and synchronization systems based on optical pulse trains generated from ultralow-noise mode-locked lasers.

articleTitle: Coherent Detection in Submarine Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We discuss potential advantages of coherent detection in reducing required OSNR or increasing spectral efficiency of current submarine optical systems. We investigate the impact of carrier-phase-estimation schemes and fiber nonlinearity on coherent-detection performance.

articleTitle: Integrated Microfluidic Photonic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Fluid-filled on-chip polymer lenses incorporated into a microfluidic flow cytometer are used to localize excitation and allow for multi-parameter measurements. These improvements lower signal variation while maintaining throughput in a low-powered, disposable polymer chip device.

articleTitle: LDPC-Coded Modulation for High-Speed Optical Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Several LDPC-coded modulation schemes enabling ges100 Gb/s transmission using commercially available components operating 40 Giga symbols/s are presented: (a) coded orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), (b) bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM), and (c) multilevel coding (MLC).

articleTitle: Generation of 100+++ Gbit/s signals using multilevel modulation formats
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Multilevel modulation formats are used as the enabling technology to obtain 120 Gbit/s per channel bit rates, and 240 Gbit/s when polarisation multiplexing is added. Using OTDM, this can be extended even further.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh dynamic-range distance measurement using a femtosecond frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report a compact optical distance meter using intermode beats of a fiber-delivered frequency comb. We realized micrometer agreement over hundreds of meters to a length-measuring laser interferometer which is the reference standard at NMIJ/AIST.

articleTitle: Fiber Nonlinearity Mitigation by Electronic and Optical Techniques
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We discuss various electronic and optical techniques to reduce the impact of fiber nonlinearity and improve other system performance aspects in the context of optically-routed networks. Main differences between optical and electronic techniques are highlighted.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electronic Equalization in Coherent Receivers with Complex Modulation Schemes
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We propose a post detection equalizer design for complex multilevel modulation and coherent I/Q-detection and investigate the performance in terms of dispersion tolerance for both linear and nonlinear (Kerr effect) fiber effects.

articleTitle: An Extraordinary New Class of Electro-Optic Materials: Binary Chromophore Glasses
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Binary chromophore organic glasses, a new class of electro-optic (EO) materials, has recently shown to exhibit EO activities of 300-500 pm/V at telecommunication wavelengths. These composite materials also exhibit low optical loss (2 dB/cm) and good thermal stability (glass transition temperatures of 200degC). This article considers the characteristics of these materials responsible for these extraordinary properties.

articleTitle: Enhanced Band-Edge and Defect-Mode Effects of Laser Action in Chiral Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A two-photon confocal microscope lithography technique was used to fabricate nano-defect structure in the chiral helicoidal system and higher-order confinement structure based on the chiral liquid crystals. Tunable defect mode and laser actions on this nano-modulated chiral helix structure have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Mechanotransduction in Endothelial Cells: Role of Laser and Electro-Optics in Mechanobiology
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Summary form only given. Mechanotransduction in vascular endothelial cells (ECs) varies with the directions of the shear stress or mechanical strain and plays a significant role in the modulation of cellular functions in health and disease. Most studies on these signaling processes have been conducted by using biochemical or molecular procedures to examine a large number of cells subjected to controlled experimental conditions and then made into a lysate composed of all the cells studied. With the increasing recognition of the spatial and temporal variations in the mechanotransduction processes, however, it is necessary to have technologies that would enable investigations on single cells and subcellular components in 4D, i.e., in 3D space and with time-dependent dynamics. There are a large number of possibilities to apply laser and electro-optics to elucidate molecular and cellular processes in health and disease

articleTitle: Nanosecond cw Visible-IR All-Optical Switching and Nonlinear Transmission with a Nonlinear Organic Optical Liquid in Bulk and Guided Wave Geometry
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Passive all-optical protection against such multiple time-scales and extremely broadband intense light sources is rather challenging due to the fact that an optical limiting mechanism that is efficient in one time scale usually become rather inefficient in another time scale. Nonlinear absorptions such as Two-Photon absorptions [TPA] and Excited State absorption [ESA] that are effective for limiting nanosecond laser pulses simply do not work in the microseconds and longer time scales as a result of the reduction in power/intensity for the same energy flux. In these time scales, a variety of approaches and materials, including dye-doped aligned nematic liquid crystals, have emerged as promising alternatives [1, 2]. In this presentation, we describe another promising organic material that enables all-optical switching in an extremely wide time scales spanning sub-nanoseconds to cw regime a nonlinear neat organic liquid (L34) in bulk or wave-guided [fiber core] structure. In the visible spectrum [400 -700 nm], quantitative z-scan and pump-probe techniques [3, 4] have shown that in the sub-nanosecond time scales, the dominant nonlinear absorption processes are two-photon coupled to excited state absorption processes characterized by an intrinsic two photon absorption coefficient of ~5 cm/GW, and an intensity dependent effective two-photon absorption coefficient that can be over 200 cm/GW. For longer time scales, the transparency of the liquid allows doping with appropriate absorbers to generate efficient thermal/density and nonlinear scattering effects [as well as guided mode extinction in fiber geometry] for all-optical switching

articleTitle: High-performance Ultra Violet 4H-SiC Avalanche Photodiode detectors
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: 4H-SiC avalanche photodiodes are studied in both linear and Geiger mode. Single photon detection efficiency of 14% is reported in Geiger mode.

articleTitle: Enhanced Design of OptoFluidic Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced design of opto-fluidic microscopy (OFM) with significant improvement. OFM is a novel optical imaging device that can be directly integrated into a microfluidic network, and can therefore enable high resolution and on-chip imaging of biological samples that are flowing in microfluidic channels. The main advantages of OFM are its very compact miniaturized design, low cost, high throughput, and its non destructive nature of optical probing. But the key advantage of this optical imaging device is its ability to capture high resolution (750 nm) images although it is free from any bulk optics (lenses). Instead of bulk optics, OFM is based on a nanohole array defined in an opaque metallic layer that is patterned onto the floor of the microfluidic channel and then mounted on top of a one dimensional CCD or photodiode array.

articleTitle: PQ-based derivatives doped PMMA photopolymers for holographic data storage
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We report our investigation on several poly(methyl methacrylate)(PMMA) photopolymers doped with different 9,10-phenanthrenequinone based derivatives for holographic data storage. By introducing different kinds of the functional groups on the doped elements, we could tailor the holographic characteristics of the materials.

articleTitle: High "intrinsic" first hyperpolarizability by modulating the conjugation path between donor and acceptor
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Summary form only given. The authors report on a series of chromophores that have been synthesized with a modulated conjugation path between donor and acceptor. Hyper-Rayleigh scattering measurements of the best molecules show an enhanced hyperpolarizability that breaches the apparent limit. They show the molecular structures and a plot of the static first hyperpolarizability normalized to the fundamental limit of the hyperpolarizability. It is clear that for the first time, the "Kuzyk gap" is breached. While our best measured values of the hyperpolarizability are still more than an order of magnitude from the fundamental limit, our design strategy appears to be a promising new paradigm for making better molecular materials for electro-optical modulation.

articleTitle: Nanoimprinted photonic crystals enhanced light emitters via surface plasmon
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A method to enhance the light-emission efficiency of organic thin films via nanoimprinted photonic crystals and coupled surface plasmons is reported. The photonic crystal (PhC) is made in a polymer film doped with rhodamine 6G. The photoluminescence (PL) spectra of the sample are investigated.

articleTitle: Self-healing of polymer lasers and two-photon absorbers
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper reports the photodegradation and recovery of two-photon fluorescence (TPF) in the chromophore AF455 doped in poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) polymer, known to have a large two-photon absorption cross-section and a promising optical material for many applications. The self-healing of amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in the DO11 system is also analysed.

articleTitle: Widely Tunable (1.0-1.7 μm) Yb-doped Fiber Mode-Locked Laser Source with ˜100 fs Pulse Widths based on Raman Frequency Shift
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A widely tunable (1.0-1.7 μm) femtosecond laser source based on Raman induced frequency shift in a photonic crystal fiber pumped by a Yb-doped mode-locked fiber laser is presented. The output pulses are ˜100 fs wide with ˜0.5 nJ pulse energy.

articleTitle: Photonic metamaterials new opportunities for nanoimprint
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This article presents a short discussion on the fabrication of photonic metamaterials. The method of choice for fabricating metamaterials is still electron beam lithography despite its intrinsic drawbacks like long writing time and high operation costs. Thus only small areas can be structured within reasonable time and at reasonable costs. Another way to fabricate high-quality photonic metamaterials on a macroscopic scale is provided by interference lithography which allows structuring huge areas. Another promising technique to achieve large-scale, high-quality metamaterials is nanoimprint lithography, which was recently applied to fabricate photonic metamaterials.

articleTitle: CMOS Chemical and Biochemical Sensors using Nanostructured Materials
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A review of the recent progress in complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) biological and chemical optical sensors using nanostructured materials is presented. Fabrication details of a xerogel based glucose sensor and a photonic bandgap based chemical vapor sensor are also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Spectral narrowing of emission in self-assembled colloidal photonic superlattices
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper reports on the influence of a well-designed passband in the stopband of a suitably engineered self-assembled colloidal photonic crystal superlattice on the steady-state and time-resolved emission properties of infiltrated fluorophores. Efficient all-optical integrated circuits can be realized from photonic superlattices and heterostructures.

articleTitle: Frequency Measurement of an Optical Lattice Clock
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A frequency measurement system is developed away from a National Metrological Institute with a frequency link to International Atomic Time (TAI). The absolute frequency of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> -<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> clock transition of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Sr lattice clock is determined to be 429,228,004,229,875(4) Hz. The frequency measurement system is being further improved by introducing an optical fiber link and by upgrading the GPS link.

articleTitle: High Resolution Optical Waveform Sampling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Techniques to analyze optical waveforms with high resolution are discussed. Emphasis is on all-optical sampling that offers high resolution with excellent sensitivity.

articleTitle: Realtime Optical Synchronous QPSK Transmission with DFB lasers
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of the components required to realize a 10 Gbaud synchronous optical quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) transmission system. These are a 5 bit 10 Gsamples/s analog-to-digital converter and a digital signal processing unit for carrier and data recovery.

articleTitle: Practical Challenges for Electronic Dispersion Compensation in CMOS
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Compared to fractional tap-spacing, baud-rate EDC offers simpler tap-weight adaptation while suffering little performance penalty. Unfortunately, the popular CMOS traveling-wave filter provides insufficient bandwidth for baud-rate tap-spacing.

articleTitle: Origination and Tooling of Optical Structures on Planar and 3D Surfaces for Mass Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Processes for tooling of larger arrangements of refractive and diffractive structures on planar surfaces as well as details of the fabrication of gratings combined with lenses are discussed and examples for specific applications are shown.

articleTitle: Subretinal Implantable Micro Photodetector Array
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: A subretinal implant device, microphotodiode array, which can partly imitate the function of photoreceptor cells, was presented. Process to fabricate the MPDA and characteristics of the MPDA in vivo were described.

articleTitle: Optical Waveform Generation, Measurement, and Utilization
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This talk outlines the DARPA optical arbitrary waveform generation program. Fundamental application classes are mentioned, and the scientific motivation for each developed to indicate overall goals, prospects for technology development, and insertion into specific devices.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of organic solid-state lasers using imprint technologies
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: This work has demonstrated the feasibility of both UV and thermal nanoimprinting as fabrication tools for organic laser resonators. In conjunction with the realized waveguide coupling, an important step towards an integrated organic laser source for optical sensor systems is presented.

articleTitle: Metastable States of MLSE Receiver Induced by Extreme PMD Conditions
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We have measured the performance of a 10 Gb/s receiver incorporating maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (MLSE) under conditions of severe polarization-mode dispersion (PMD). We find that certain trajectories of PMD evolution can lead to metastable states of receiver operation.

articleTitle: Micro/Nano-Imprinting of Polymer Optical Waveguides for Optical Printed Circuit Board (O-PCB) Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We present a review of our research results on the thermal or ultraviolet (UV) imprinting of micro/nano-scale polymer optical waveguides of diverse nature and dimensions for the fabrication and integration of an optical micro-system that we call optical printed circuit board (O-PCB), which are made in hard and flexible forms of generic and application-specific nature. Micro/nano-photonic devices, like micro-lasers, sensors, couplers, splitters, filters, micro-ring/racetrack resonator devices, photonic crystal devices, and plasmonic devices are interconnected and integrated using imprinted polymer waveguides to perform the functions of sensing, storing, processing, transporting, switching, and distributing optical signals on the O-PCBs. We describe the detailed process of designing, imprinting, fabricating, and integrating waveguides and discuss on the scientific and engineering issues and challenges thereof.

articleTitle: All-Order PMD Compensation of Sub-picosecond Optical Pulses with Arbitrary Input States of Polarization
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: We demonstrate full compensation of ~800 fs optical pulses distorted by all-order polarization mode dispersion effects to ~10 ps by applying polarization switching, wavelength-parallel polarization sensing, and ultrafast optical pulse shaping techniques.

articleTitle: Modulation Coding for Optical Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: The effect of a modulation code generated by a "forbidden list" of input sequences on the performance of an optical receiver that uses a fixed state Viterbi algorithm is analyzed.

articleTitle: Laser-Ablated Microfluidics for Nanoflow Life Science Measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: An overview of the laser ablation fabrication method for polymer microfluidic chips is presented with a discussion of some of the interesting and useful designs and applications of the technology along with a presentation of measurement results for some life science applications.

publicationTitle: 2007 Digest of the IEEE/LEOS Summer Topical Meetings
abstract: Presents the foreword from the conference proceedings.
